# Markdown Instructions

Write human-readable raw Markdown. Documentation must remain clear and easy to follow when viewed as source text, without requiring rendered output.

## Structure

- Use descriptive headings to make the document easy to scan.
- Keep paragraphs focused and reasonably short.
- Use lists when the items are genuinely parallel or sequential.
- Use tables only when they make comparisons or mappings clearer.
- Keep heading levels in a logical order without skipping levels.

## Formatting

- Prefer simple Markdown over HTML or renderer-specific features.
- Leave a blank line around headings, lists, tables, and fenced code blocks.
- Use descriptive link text instead of bare URLs where practical.
- Keep table source readable and avoid overly wide tables when prose or a list would be clearer.
- Use fenced code blocks with a language identifier when the language is known.
- Write one sentence per line, do not split sentences across multiple lines unless they are very long or contain multiple clauses.

## Content

- Lead with the information the reader needs to understand the section.
- Use plain, precise language and define project-specific terminology.
- Distinguish implemented behavior from requirements, proposals, and unresolved work.
- Link factual technical claims to repository files or relevant project discussions when evidence is available.
- Do not add placeholder sections or unsupported claims merely to complete a template.
